summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for question answering)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Sea Mystery" by Freeman Wills Crofts (Inspector French detective story; Gutenberg 72771)

**Ch 1 – Mr. Morgan Meets Tragedy.** Burry Inlet, south coast of Wales, late September evening. Mr. Morgan (small, clean-shaven, baggy Norfolk suit; manager of tin-plate works at Burry Port) fishes with son Evan (14, at school ~3 yrs, back to school next day). Catch: two mackerel. Lines snag on an object ~20 ft (3.5 fathoms) down; grappling-iron hooks a wooden crate (3ft x 2ft x 2ft, cross-pieces; flukes caught under upper cross-piece). They tow it to Burry Port lifeboat slip. Mr. Morgan takes bearings (signal post on railway in line with west gable of large white house on hill; tall mill chimney in line with pier-head beacon). That night Mr. Morgan prises lid with cold chisel; sees body (man in underclothes, advanced decomposition). He hides it from Evan, reports to Sergeant Nield at police station. Nield, Constable Williames, Smith, Watson; coastguard Tom Manners. Crate hauled to station. Chief Constable Major Lloyd (Llandilo), Superintendent Griffiths (Llanelly), Dr. Crowth (police surgeon), Dr. Wilbraham. Body: face battered beyond recognition; death from blow to back of head; dead ~5–6 weeks. Triangular birthmark on back of left arm. No labels; label tacks show absent label; steel bar ~14 in (2-inch shafting, ~3–4 stone) as weight; 14 small holes (~1/6 in) at diagonal corners. Chief Constable calls in Scotland Yard.

**Ch 2 – Inspector French Gets Busy.** Inspector Joseph French (short, stout, keen blue eyes, twinkle) arrives from Paddington. Method: be friendly, lead rather than drive. Examines body, sketches birthmark; notes socks (left toe darned with wrong-shade wool). Theory: crate floated (holes admit water slowly); weights: crate+body+bar = 406 lb; displacement 985 lb; buoyancy 579 lb; Molesworth formula gives ~1 hour to sink. Speaks with Dr. Crowth (cause: blow with soft instrument, then face smashed post-mortem; Crowth says death 35–40 days earlier). French cites Inspector Burnley's Cask case (France to London). Asks Nield for Molesworth's Pocket Book.

**Ch 3 – Experimental Detection.** Manners (ex-Royal Navy, from Shoreditch). Tide tables: possible dates 21st/22nd/23rd August (neap). Loughor road bridge (ferro-concrete, ~300 yds) best launch point. Experiment next day (Thursday, 9:30 AM), crate loaded with shingle, dropped from Loughor bridge, floats 1 hr 7 min, passes within 50 yards of original spot. Lorry/crane theory. Circular → Neath: Constable David Jenkins saw a breakdown lorry with crane and tarpaulin-covered crate ~8 pm Mon 22 Aug, two miles north of Neath (lane through spinney, near Pontardawe direction); driver ~middle height, stout, reddish hair, high colour, glasses, said going Swansea→Merthyr Tydfil.

**Ch 4 – A Change of Venue.** Superintendent Howells (Swansea). Sightings: lorry in Morriston ~5 pm 22 Aug; 10 am 23 Aug on Pontardulais road; 12:30 am at Gorseinon lane. Llewellyn's Garage, Fisher Street, Swansea (Stepney Motor Car Co.): lorry hired by letter from "John F. Stewart, St. Pancras Hotel" (typewritten, black ribbon), deposit £300, hire £5; returned next day; driver paid back £295. Driver: red hair, glasses, untidy, looked like labourer. Goods: Morriston Road GWR Goods Station; porter; clerk Evans; waybill: "Mr. James S. Stephenson, GWR Goods Station, Morriston Road, Swansea. To be called for." Sender: The Veda Office Equipment Manufacturing Co. Ltd., Ashburton, South Devon (invoiced 16 Aug, arrived Swansea 20 Aug). Crate contained duplicator. Ashburton sergeant confirms. French suspects body put in during lorry run; later gorseinon sighting suggests lorry stationary 9:30–12:30 so body maybe from Devon.

**Ch 5 – Messrs. Berlyn and Pyke.** Ashburton (T-shaped town, Silver Tiger hotel). Sergeant Daw. Veda Works (North Street). Charles Berlyn (junior partner, ~40, fair/reddish hair, blue eyes, high colour) and Stanley Pyke (engineer/travelling rep, ~35, sallow, brown eyes/hair), vanished 15 Aug night while driving to Tavistock Urban District Council meeting (office appliances). Car found 8 miles out on moor near Two Bridges road; magneto short circuit; footsteps to Colonel Domlio's house (Torview), ¾ mile across moor. Quagmire (mire) risk. Torquay Western Morning News files read.

**Ch 6 – The Despatch of the Crate.** Letter dated 12 August from Euston Hotel, signed "James S. Stephenson," typed, disguised signature, for Veda No.3 duplicator (~2 cwt), 220V DC, money order £62.10.0; to be kept at Morriston Road GWR goods station. Packing: packer John Puddicoombe; carter; night watchman John/Gurney (old, goatee, wizened; works 7 pm–6 am). Crate left in packing shed overnight 15/16 Aug, taken 16 Aug 11:35 goods train to Plymouth then Swansea. Fogden = sales manager (youngish, pleasant).

**Ch 7 – Dartmoor.** Daw; Makepeace garage (proprietor John Makepeace; son); Berlyn's car (blue fifteen-twenty Mercury). Magneto armature burnt out (Ardlo magneto; Ardlo factory in Bermondsey). French and Daw drive to crash site: road ~8 miles out; Fox Tor Mire; Colonel Domlio (senior partner, ~45, entomologist, lives alone with servants: John Burt, Sarah Burt, Coombe chauffeur, Mee gardener). Test drive 63 min to Tavistock. Radiator cooling test: 3.5 hrs. French's time-table reconstruction. Conclusion: car couldn't have carried body; breakdown probably genuine.

**Ch 8 – A Fresh Start.** Daw on Berlyn: married Phyllis (née Considine) ~4–5 yrs ago; house "Soller" on Buckland road; Phyllis's affairs with Pyke (ended ~4 months before), Colonel Domlio rumoured. Pyke's cousin Jefferson Pyke (Argentine). Lizzie Johnston, maid; French examines grey socks: Phyllis never darned; Lizzie darns. Daw explains mire physics: can't sink a body.

**Ch 9 – A Step Forward.** Mrs. Billing, Pyke's landlady (talkative, 17b? Kepple Street later; East Street Ashburton). Recognises underclothes, darned grey sock, buttons, cuff-links. Mr. Jefferson Pyke (London, 17b Kepple Street, off Russell Square) identifies birthmark (triangular, left upper arm). French concludes body = Stanley Pyke. Berlyn suspected. Phyllis Berlyn at 70b Park Walk, Chelsea.

**Ch 10 – London's Further Contribution.** Phyllis interview (denies affair; claims Berlyn innocent). Ardlo magneto expert Mr. Illingworth: breakdown could be faked by needle in winding but not instantly; spare magneto idea. Magneto spare ordered by "Henry Armstrong, Westcliff Hotel, Bristol," typed letter, sent to St. David's Station parcels office, Exeter. Inspector Tanner (Yard).

**Ch 11 – John Gurney, Night Watchman.** Gurney's cottage; roses (La France). Gurney confesses he slept after supper that night (Peter Small the fireman woke him). Supper doped; key to office gate. Experiment: French tests timing from office door ring to wicket.

**Ch 12 – The Duplicator.** French examines stock cards: 54 leg castings; doctored entries (6 altered to 8 — two castings "removed"). Forges four cards. Sketches parts. Lizzie's fiancé Alfred "Alf" Beer, ex-packer, dismissed by Berlyn; overheard Phyllis and Pyke in shrubbery ("'e knows"). Berlyn theory built.

**Ch 13 – The Accomplice?** Domlio theory. Interview: Domlio says he was in his study all evening. Servants (Burt, Mrs. Burt) show fear. Coombe: car out, 2 gallons petrol, mud. French hides at gate, sees Domlio drive out.

**Ch 14 – French Turns Fisherman.** Domlio admits drive: lost miniature (wife's portrait, gold, diamonds) at Chagford-area rabbit hole; claims returned ~2 am. Well at Torview: French/Daw fish with hooks, pull up a black coat (tailor tab: "R. Shrubsole & Co., Newton Abbot"; brown tweed purple line). Shrubsole's: suit made for Stanley Pyke among four names.

**Ch 15 – Blackmail.** Pump removal from well (42 ft deep, 12 ft water). Recovered: waistcoat, trousers, shoes, duplicator small parts. Domlio's account: Phyllis twisted ankle, photographer blackmail letter ("X.Y.Z.", Upper Merton glen, Chagford–Gidleigh road, Dobson's Spinney). Domlio: "My late wife" miniature. Domlio not arrested; watched.

**Ch 16 – Certainty at Last.** Dr. Lancaster and Mrs. Lancaster: Phyllis left party ~20 min. Berlyn's bicycle (Swift, no. 35,721, bought from Makepeace) missing; pawned in Plymouth. Plymouth Superintendent. Ideas: Berlyn vs Pyke dilemma; French suspects Phyllis & Pyke / Jefferson.

**Ch 17 – "Danger!"** Phyllis interview (French bluffs). Phyllis sends telephone message via Ganope (news agent, 27 Oakley Street, Russell Street) to "James Hurley" at Wright's (Bedford Place/Ivy Street). Boy to Kepple Street: "Danger. Meet me to-night at old time and place." Jefferson Pyke's account of trip: Flintshire (Bibby Line, Birkenhead→Marseilles), San Remo, Grasse (Metropole), Nîmes, Arles, Avignon, Regina/Houston hotels in Paris.

**Ch 18 – On Hampstead Heath.** French shadows Pyke to Hampstead Heath (Jack Straw's Castle, hollow). Overhears Phyllis and Pyke. Pyke "confesses" plan. Pyke escapes via roof from Kepple Street; Phyllis locked in Park Walk escapes too.

**Ch 19 – The Bitterness of Death.** Typewriter Corona Four; Vera Welsh (landlady's daughter, typist, Tottenham Court Road hardware shop) typed copy of tenders on Pyke's machine; matches magneto/duplicator letters. Pyke on Flintshire, Hawkins purser; Houston hotel (Nos. 346/351). Taximan William Service: Pyke + Phyllis taken to Victory Place, Elephant & Castle (flat No. 19, "Mr. and Mrs. Perrin"). French confronts "Pyke" in flat (actually Stanley Pyke, disguised); pistol; struggle; Phyllis throttles French; Carter arrives.

**Ch 20 – Conclusion.** French realises victim was Berlyn (?) — the impersonation: Stanley posed as Jefferson, Jefferson had died at Nice (appendicitis). Stanley and Phyllis executed some weeks after assizes. Full plot: Berlyn murdered by Stanley with Phyllis's help; crate; duplicator; magneto; well; forged letters; Jefferson's money forged sale.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Bindle: Some Chapters in the Life of Joseph Bindle" by Herbert Jenkins (1916)

**Foreword** – author H. J.; Blackwood's suggested book; 12 Arundel Place, Haymarket.

**Ch I – The Bindles at Home.** Blue Boar pub, Hammersmith. Bindle (small, bald, red nose, great heart; furniture-remover; "little joke"). Ginger (freckles, gloomy, misanthropic; no kids; 3 babies; married Chiswick). Bindle's father drank himself to death "keepin' the chill out." Mrs. Bindle (Lizzie, sandy hair, sharp, religious, Alton Road Chapel; hymn "Gospel Bells"; cleans, parlour with antimacassars). Bindle's solution: "tack," "Gospel Bells," tin of salmon. Fenton Street home (half-house, Fulham). Bindle lies: night watchman job; pawns clock for 7 shillings. Bindle's "little jokes"; "Lorst yer job?" Mrs. Bindle's sister Martha married Alfred Hearty (greengrocer, Fulham High Street, 530). Bindle's fulfilled plan to steal ("steal" thought).

**Ch II – A Nocturnal Adventure.** Finds keys of Professor Sylvanus Conti (13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, West Kensington); has duplicates made (1s), dresses in bandages, enters flat. Conti (born Willie Wilkins, Bermondsey/Bow; hypnotist; rival "John Gibson, the English Mesmerist"). Conti catches Bindle, handcuffs him, hypnotises him, writes note to police; Bindle carries note; returns property by post.

**Ch III – The Hypnotic Fiasco.** Bindle delivers note to police; a workman takes it. Conti's hypnosis fiasco in West London Police Court; magistrate: "someone who is something of a humorist." Conti loses reputation.

**Ch IV – The Heartys at Home.** Mr. Alfred Hearty (religious, woolly voice, walrus-like moustache, sucks moustache loudly; gives "pious smile"). Mrs. Martha Hearty (fat, wheezes, laughs with Bindle). Daughter Millie (18; loves "Uncle Joe"; cat "Tibbins"). Sunday evening hymns: "Pull for the Shore, Sailors," "Gospel Bells." Bindle sings to ruin them. Lemon flavour hated by Bindle.

**Ch V – Bindle Tries a Change of Work.** Splendid Hotel night painting job; foreman (Sanders) insults; Bindle sabotages numbers on doors of No. 1 East corridor (paint). Chambermaid ("Ruthie") banter.

**Ch VI – The Hotel Corridor.** Night-time chaos: wrong room numbers, man in bath-robe, Frenchman "Vingt-quatre," clergyman (Rev. in nightshirt), "Fighting parson." Fireman restores numbers. Mrs. Bindle hits foreman Sanders with broom.

**Ch VII – Bindle Commits an Indiscretion.** Millie + Charlie Dixon (shipping-office clerk; typist Millie at wholesale draper). Bindle at Putney Pavilion; Millie's romance; Hearty knocks into Millie; Bindle befriends. Bindle's grudge.

**Ch VIII – The Great Conspiracy.** Barton Bridge Temperance Fete (Harridge's Stores; Bindle in charge of lemonade; secretly spiked with spirit "distilled mead" from Dick Little, doctor's son). Lady Knob-Kerrick (Castle; hostile). Rev. Mr. Slocum (vicar), Rev. Andrew McFie (Scots Congregational).

**Ch IX – The Temperance Fete.** Chaos: hose, police, Morris dancers, maypole; Mr. Wace; McFie with fire-hose; Bindle leaves with "pure alcohol mixed with distilled mead."

**Ch X – Mr. Hearty Prays for Bindle.** Mrs. Bindle: "a brother fallen by the wayside, a wheat-ear among thorns." Bindle goes to Dick Little's Chelsea flat (550 Beaufort Mansions); Tim's (St. Timothy's Hospital) friends.

**Ch XI – Mr. Hearty Becomes Extremely Unpopular.** Fake advert "DOG WANTED … 530 Fulham High Street"; dog Lily; Bindle's mass chaos; traffic jam; pineapple gift.

**Ch XII – Bindle Agrees to Become a Millionaire.** Reginald "Gravy" Graves (grocer's son, Bingley; St. Joseph's College, Oxford; uncle "Josiah Williams" Australian millionaire invented). Plot: Dick and Tom Little, Travers, Guggers.

**Ch XIII – Oxford's Welcome to Bindle.** Station reception (kangaroo-costume "Horace Trent" cox); Bungem's supper; Bindle's speech about Tom Graves grocer; Graves flees.

**Ch XIV – Mr. Hearty Gives a Party.** Hearty party; Rev. Edward Winch (missionary); Bindle's speech; Mr. Sopley (pastor).

**Ch XV – Bindle and the German Menace.** Little Compton, Suffolk; Holmleigh (Mr. Richard Miller, gun collection); Mr. Gandy (Dove and Easel); Sir Charles Custance (magistrate, invasion fears), Sergeant Wrannock; Mr. Greenhales; foreman Brooks catches all three in van.

**Ch XVI – The Amateur Detectives.** Foreman's night-watch; capture; Mr. Miller; Germans fears undone.

**Ch XVII – Bindle Makes a Mistake.** Moving furniture from 181 (wrong key: 131) Branksome Road to 33 Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick; Rogers family (Railton-Rogers, seven kids); Grangers; Bindle sacked.

**Ch XVIII – Bindle Assists in an Elopement.** Bindle joins special constables; Dick Little elopes with Ethel Knob-Kerrick (Guggers' Rolls-Royce); Lady Knob-Kerrick captures Bindle; Bindle extracts £5.

**Ch XIX – The Scarlet Horse Coterie.** Friday pub circle (Ginger, Huggles, Wilkes, Ruddy Bill, Tom Cave, Weary); Bindle on war; Ginger enlists.

**Ch XX – Millie Leaves Home.** Hearty row; Millie leaves; Bindle takes her to Aunt Elizabeth (Mrs. Bindle); Mrs. Bindle sobs.

**Ch XXI – Conclusion.** Millie engaged to Charlie Dixon (enlisted); Littles' Chelsea Palace Mansions flat; Bindle's closing.

**Other titles listed**: The Night Club, Adventures of Bindle, Mrs. Bindle, The Bindles on the Rocks, John Dene of Toronto, Malcolm Sage Detective, Patricia Brent Spinster, The Rain-Girl, The Return of Alfred.
